title: Sheaves of modules on a scheme have enough injectives
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ the abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules on the underlying topological space of $X$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ has enough injectives: every $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ admits a monomorphism $\mathcal F\to\mathcal I$ into an injective object $\mathcal I$ of $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. (Stacks states and proves this for an arbitrary ringed space, with functorial injective embeddings.)

source.place: Injectives, Lemma 01DI (lemma-sheaves-modules-space); used in Cohomology of Sheaves, Section 01EO (literature/stacks-project/cohomology.tex, the paragraph defining $H^i(X,\mathcal F)$ by an injective resolution)

proof.text: The opens of a scheme X : Scheme.{u} form a small site, and its structure sheaf is X.ringCatSheaf. The Grothendieck-abelian assertion of [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] is already proved independently of its additional localized-generator clause by SheafOfModules.isGrothendieckAbelian in WeilConjectures.Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.Abelian. Apply that proved theorem to X.ringCatSheaf to obtain IsGrothendieckAbelian.{u} X.Modules. The small-site sheafification hypotheses are inferred by Mathlib; X.Modules is definitionally SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf.

Apply [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives], namely the Mathlib instance CategoryTheory.IsGrothendieckAbelian.enoughInjectives, to this Grothendieck abelian structure. This gives EnoughInjectives X.Modules and hence an injective presentation of every module sheaf, including on an empty scheme.

proof_origin.place: SheafOfModules.isGrothendieckAbelian, specialized to X.ringCatSheaf; Mathlib CategoryTheory/Abelian/GrothendieckCategory/EnoughInjectives.lean, instance IsGrothendieckAbelian.enoughInjectives. Shorter established route to Stacks 01DI; no change to the unit statement or its realized steps.
